name: llama.cpp
summary: A C/C++ local inference runtime that loads GGUF model artifacts, evaluates ggml graphs across selectable hardware backends, and exposes command-line and HTTP serving interfaces.

features.name: GGUF model artifact boundary
features.description: The repository provides GGUF conversion and model tooling, and its CLI/server workflows load model artifacts identified by local paths or Hugging Face model references.
benefits: Separates model metadata and tensor data from the runtime executable
Supports a portable artifact boundary for local and hosted model sources
costs: Artifact format and model-family support constrain interoperability
Loading and quantization choices remain tied to available memory and backend support

features.name: ggml graph runtime with selectable backends
features.description: llama.cpp builds inference from ggml tensor operations and can dispatch work through CPU, CUDA, Metal, HIP, Vulkan, SYCL, and other configured backends, including CPU/GPU hybrid execution.
benefits: Reuses one graph-oriented execution model across hardware targets
Allows partial offload when a model does not fit entirely in accelerator memory
costs: Backend capabilities and numerical behavior are hardware- and build-dependent
Graph placement and transfer boundaries add configuration and resource complexity

features.name: Grammar-constrained decoding
features.description: The project includes GBNF grammar tooling and exposes grammar-constrained completion paths, allowing a decoder to restrict generated token sequences to a supplied formal grammar.
benefits: Moves selected output-shape constraints into the decoding boundary
Supports structured generation without requiring a separate post-parser
costs: Grammar construction and tokenization compatibility affect reachable outputs
Constraint processing adds state and can exclude otherwise likely continuations

features.name: CLI and OpenAI-compatible HTTP serving
features.description: The repository supplies command-line tools and a server tool that loads a model and serves completion/chat-style requests through an HTTP API described as OpenAI-compatible.
benefits: Provides both embedded/local command execution and a process-level service boundary
Lets existing OpenAI-shaped clients call a local inference process
costs: The service inherits single-process model, memory, and scheduling constraints
API compatibility does not imply identical model, tokenizer, or sampling semantics

mathematical_views.question: How does a serialized model artifact determine the tensor graph and parameters evaluated by the runtime?
assumptions: The artifact metadata and tensors are compatible with the selected model implementation
Conversion and loading are modeled as a boundary before graph execution
The view abstracts file layout and allocator details

mathematical_views.question: Which graph operations and tensor regions can be mapped from an abstract ggml graph onto heterogeneous backend resources?
assumptions: Each configured backend implements the operation subset required by the graph
Transfers and partial offload are explicit transitions
This view does not claim performance equivalence across backends

mathematical_views.question: How does a grammar restrict the set of token transitions available during autoregressive decoding?
assumptions: The grammar state is updated after each accepted token
Tokenizer and grammar terminals are compatible
The view abstracts logits, sampling policy, and model state outside allowed-token filtering

benefits: One graph model across hardware backends

costs: Grammar/tokenizer state and reduced reachable outputs

benefits: Local service boundary with familiar API shape
